limits: Python and SQLite on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with SQLite 3.39.0 (Pyodide 0.28.2), while the research behind the page ran under Python 3.14.6 with SQLite 3.53.1. Eight examples were rewritten for research version 1.0.3 so that they give the same result in both: LargeDataLimits, NotADatabaseFile, CloseAndWarnings, BooleanAndDates, SqliteVersion, NamedPlaceholders, MealIngredients and InMemoryDatabase. Each was run in the browser and compared with its stored result. The page's Chapter examples are the 25 code examples of the deck, taken from the deck's chapter-code manifest (same code, same order); each was run in the browser's Python (Pyodide 0.28.2) and its result compared with the manifest's recorded result before the page was built.

Recorded, not run: two examples start another program, which a browser cannot do, so they show the output recorded under Python 3.14.6 and are labelled so: SqliteCli, PythonShell (the sqlite3 shell of release 3.54.0 and python -m sqlite3).

The book's database: five examples open sweigartcats.db from the online materials of the 3rd edition (a zip of 7,759,877 bytes, SHA-256 dac627e807f69ee14913ba621a15dec1f98db739d76939555ba5360d05eba916). The research scripts download it; a browser page cannot depend on a download, so this page holds the file itself (24,576 bytes, SHA-256 starting 41f0d0b5bc2e, 100 cats and 291 vaccination rows), writes it to the browser's temporary folder, and each example still checks the hash before it opens the file. The zip carries no licence file; the book's text is free to read under a Creative Commons licence, and the course owner should confirm that this file may be kept on the page.

NOT EXECUTED: the three graphical applications (DB Browser for SQLite, SQLiteStudio now named Letos, DBeaver Community), the installers of the sqlite3 shell for Windows and macOS and sudo apt install sqlite3, the book's figures as drawn, and the Practice Programs as the book's readers would write them (only their data and queries were run).

What the public sites answered on 2026-10-12 is in live_observations_v1_0_0.json: the chapter's page (status 200, 113,075 bytes, equal to the digest in the book's ontology), sqlite.org's newest release (3.54.0, dated 2026-10-09) and the pages of the three database tools. It is one request each, on one day, and nothing re-checks it.

One program was run under 10 interpreters (3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.16, 3.14.0, 3.14.1, 3.14.2, 3.14.3, 3.14.4, 3.14.5, 3.14.6); the SQLite library an interpreter links is the one of its build: 3.14.0 to 3.50.4, 3.14.5 to 3.53.1, 3.11.17 to 3.45.1. The items that differ between them are listed in interpreter_record_v1_0_0.json. Because of that, a result that names a version is a result for that version.
Timings: where the deck shows a time (slides 7, 15 and 18) it is one measured run on one machine and is labelled so; no example on this page prints a time.
